conviction_note: Q3 is not pre-released and the release may carry a change to the revenue guide, so I sized the move on the European new-numbers/guidance scale (6.0, above this name's 3.7-5.9% recent print reactions). The sign leans slightly negative (p_up 42): H1 revenue grew 0.9%, so the company's own 'EUR 1.2 billion' implies H2 revenue up about 6.9%, and Bunnings, the channel for the Australian business, has slowed. Three things pull back toward 50: no ad-hoc forecast change has been filed, H1 pre-tax margin of 9.7% leaves the EBT guide reachable even on lower revenue, and Hornbach's strong Jun-Aug quarter is a positive read for Western Europe. The findings sum to -1.3 and the scaled number is -0.96. They are measured apart and agree in sign.

findings.finding: The company's own numbers put the 'EUR 1.2 billion' revenue guide under strain. H1 2026 revenue was EUR 636.2m (+0.9%) and FY2025 was EUR 1,157.7m, so reaching 1.2bn needs H2 revenue of about EUR 563.8m against 527.5m, roughly +6.9%. Yet both the consensus (~1.2bn, 3 analysts) and the guide still sit at 1.2bn. So the 9M release, the scheduled moment the company narrowed its range last year, is likely to soften the revenue guide or print a 9M figure clearly off that path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 release (11.11.2025), which kept the revenue range and put earnings at the upper end: -3.7% on the day. H1 2026 (18.08.2026), guide confirmed on flat earnings: -5.9%. FY2025 ad-hoc 'above forecasts': +0.8%. Beats and confirmations have not been rewarded here.
findings.why_not_priced: Part of it is priced: the stock fell from ~75 to ~62 after H1 and sits near its 52-week low (64.5 per Lynx; 61.8 close on 27 Oct). But the visible estimates have not moved off EUR 1.2bn (aktien.guide, 3 analysts), and the stock has gained 6.35% in 5 sessions into the print on thin volume, which is not what a priced-in guidance trim looks like. If the market expected a cut, the pre-print drift would be down and the revenue consensus would sit below 1.2bn.
findings.independence: Arithmetic on the company's own H1 release and FY2025 ad-hoc (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/ad-hoc/einhell-germany-ag-preliminary-business-figures-for-2025/cefc3800-69be-4403-8511-5e36c452cbf3_en). Caveats already in the size: no Prognoseanpassung ad-hoc has been filed (https://www.eqs-news.com/search-results/?searchtype=news&searchword=Einhell), the guide says 'around' (rund), and the 9.7% H1 margin keeps EBT of ~EUR 105-108m within reach even at ~1.17bn revenue.

findings.finding: Bunnings, the channel for Einhell's Australian business (Ozito), told Wesfarmers' AGM on 29 Oct 2026 that FY27 year-to-date sales growth 'has moderated' since H2 FY26, with 'lower sales across seasonal categories ... in recent weeks'. That is the market where Einhell's H1 report already flagged a substantial earnings decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history. The H1 release, which disclosed the Australia/Argentina earnings decline, fell 5.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a counterparty statement on another continent, in a different language market, from a retailer, and no German preview of Einhell mentions it. Overseas is ~20% of group revenue (EUR 129.0m of 636.2m in H1), so it is small net of the rest. 'Recent weeks' points mostly at Einhell's Q4 outlook rather than the reported Q3.
findings.independence: The H1 report (https://www.einhell.com/fileadmin/com/investor-relations/reports/interim-reports/en/einhell-half-year-financial-report-2-2026.pdf) says Australia and Argentina 'recorded substantial declines in earnings', which is a separate company-level source for the same weakness.

findings.finding: In Einhell's core European channel, Hornbach's Jun-Aug 2026 quarter grew net sales 7.3% to EUR 1,813.7m on robust demand, especially in seasonal ranges, plus 1.3 extra selling days. Stanley Black & Decker's Q3 2026 showed Europe organic +1% with strength in Iberia, where Einhell's Spain is growing. Together these point to a Q3 Western Europe (61% of Einhell revenue) that kept growing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Western Europe growth has been the bright spot in each 2026 release (Q1 +11.2%, H1 revenue 370.0 to 388.5m), and the stock still fell on H1. Regional strength has not carried the reaction.

As reasons the DIY group names robust customer demand and a positive calendar effect of 1.3 additional selling days.]
findings.why_not_priced: It is a retailer proxy, and the overlap with Einhell's fiscal quarter is only July-August. The industry-wide BHB series for H1 was -0.4%, so Hornbach is gaining share rather than showing a rising tide. That keeps the finding small. Nothing in Einhell's tape or coverage reacted to Hornbach's print.
